title: Annotatio III §.IX close: Stillingfleet vs White before James II — Mass without Enim still latria = material idolatry; stop before §.X
pass_a_gloss: Which a few years ago gave Most Reverend Stillingfleet, disputing before James II King of Great Britain with the Jesuit White, occasion to warn that others of the Pontificians, standing by a Mass celebrated by others namely with omission of the particle Enim, and adoring the venerable (as they say), cannot even on their own hypothesis remain immune from idolatry, at least material, properly so called and in all points like Israel’s in the desert, since by the Cult of Latria they would be pursuing that which, by fault of the omitted little word enim, had not yet passed into Christ’s true body.
pass_b_english: Stillingfleet, disputing with Jesuit White before James II, used that to warn: standers at a Mass that omits Enim, adoring the ‘venerable,’ cannot escape even material idolatry on their own hypothesis.
By latria they would worship what — for want of enim — has not yet become Christ’s true body (Israel-in-the-desert parallel).
Stop before §.X (Transsubstantiation unworthy of Christ’s banquet; eliminate from the Church).
source_text: Id quod paucis abhinc annis Reverendiss. Stillingfleedio, coram Jacobo II. M. Britanniæ Rege, cum Jesuita White, disputanti, ansam dedit monendi, Pontificiorum alios, ab aliis celebratæ scil. cum omissione particulæ Enim, Missæ, adstantes ac venerabile, quod ajunt, adorantes, non posse, vel ex propria hypothesi, ab idololatria, saltem materiali, propriè interim dicta & Israëliticæ in deserto per omnia simili, immunes manere, cùm Latriæ Cultu prosequerentur id, quod, vitio omissæ voculæ enim, nondum in verum corpus Christi transiisset.
